title.narrative: Providing safe and dignified WASH and Protection services to vulnerable populations in conflict-affected areas of Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtUnprecedented rainfall events, a consequence of the climate crisis, have escalated water-related diseases, notably cholera, and acute diarrhea. Extraordinary floods, characterized by high population density of IDP and returnees, have posed formidable challenges to the operation and maintenance of water and sanitation infrastructure. fecal sludge and solid waste is compromised, leading to a substantial environmental public health impact. These challenges unfold within a context marked by a surge in people requiring water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) assistance, predominantly concentrated in the BAY States. lt/pgtltpgtYEF in partnership with GEEWCI is proposing a 6-month project aimed to improve access to safe, dignified, and sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) protection services for conflict-affected populations and host communities in Borno State Northeast Nigeria, enhancing their health, well-being, and resilience. The focus extends to IDPs, returnees, and hosting communities in the state. Additionally, the project will also provide safe and portable water points, proper hygiene and sanitation in the conflict affected communities. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtYEF and GEEWCI are requesting a total of US$150,000 from the WASH (67%) and Protection-CP (33%) sectors to implement this high-impact driven project. The project will provide access to safe clean water to the affected populations, enhance sanitation and hygiene, strengthen community coping mechanisms and resilience and prevent mortality and morbidity related to WASH diseases. Further, children and their families will have access to comprehensive child protection services including mental health and psycho-social support services.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe WASH sector will deliver on the following 4 complementary outcomes that align with the WASH cluster objectives:ltbrgt (1) Affected people have safe and equitable access to a sufficient quantity of water for domestic needs ltbrgt(2) Affected people have safe and dignified access to improved sanitation facilities ltbrgt(3) Affected people benefit from community tailored gender- and age-sensitive hygiene messages aiming at hygienic behavior and practices ltbrgt(4) Affected people benefit from basic gender- and age-sensitive hygiene items including top-ups.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe child protection component of the project will achieve the following 3 outcomes: lt/pgtltpgt1. Conflict affected children their families including unaccompanied and separated children and other children at-risks of abuse, neglect, exploitation and violence and children with disabilities as well as children formerly associated with armed groups accessed lifesaving and impact-driven comprehensive child protection services and reintegration assistance and have their well-being enhanced.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt2. Conflict affected children, caregivers/parents and the wider community members disaggregated by sex, age and disability accessed quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services and information on child protection and care and have adopted positive behaviours that prevent and respond to abuse, neglect, exploitation and violence against children. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt3. Community-based systems, government/MWASD social welfare workforce and the child protection actors or partners on the ground have been strengthened and adequately capacitated to prevent, mitigate and respond to all forms of abuse, neglect, exploitation and violence against children. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project is well positioned to safe lives and alleviate sufferings of the affected populations in Borno State. The Protection (CP) component will be implemented in Monguno and Ngala while the WASH component will be implemented in Damboa and Dikwa LGAs. The selection of the targeted communities for the response is based on the prioritized of the sectors and the severity of needs for the affected populations. Further, the project will be implemented over a period of 6 months effective 1st November 2025 to 30th April 2026. lt/pgt
